root_cause_label: Incorrect bug fix: wrong last_free_block update logic applied
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly located pool_sweep in shared_heap.c but applied an incorrect fix (updating last_free_block to p after a merge operation) that violates freelist invariants, then failed to build or verify the fix due to incomplete configure and ad-hoc compilation attempts.
t_err_evidence: Step 30: agent applies incorrect fix via sed, inserting 'last_free_block = p;' after the block-merge update. This misdiagnoses the bug; after merging two adjacent free blocks, last_free_block should remain at the run's first block (the anchor) — updating it to p breaks freelist chain integrity. The step analysis also labels this 'incorrect_fix_logic'.
t_commit_evidence: Step 46: agent runs ./apply_fix (C helper program) which successfully applies the same incorrect fix ('last_free_block = p' after merge) to the restored shared_heap.c. After this point, the incorrect fix is persisted in the file and the agent pivots to build/test attempts without reconsidering the logic, locking in the failed outcome.
t_surface_evidence: Step 52: 'gcc -c *.c' in the runtime directory produces fatal errors — 'caml/config.h:19:10: fatal error: m.h: No such file or directory' for all files — confirming the build cannot proceed without a configured environment and that no working artifact exists.
trigger_explanation: At step 27-30, the agent forms a false premise: it believes the bug is that 'last_free_block is not updated to p after merging two adjacent free blocks', but the existing code is correct in keeping last_free_block anchored at the first block of a merged run. The actual bug (per v1 annotation) is elsewhere in the sweep pointer advancement logic. This unverified causal belief leads directly to applying the wrong fix at step 30.
forewarning_evidence: Step 33: 'patch -p0 < fix.patch' reports 'Hunk #1 FAILED at 625. 1 out of 1 hunk FAILED' — an early signal that the patching approach is broken. Steps 36-39 show the code is malformed after sed edits (duplicate lines, stray expressions), indicating the edit strategy is deeply flawed. These occur before t_commit at step 46.
